evals.name: finance-group-conversion
evals.prompt: We're planning to convert finance@acme.com from a real Google Workspace user (currently a shared login several people use) into a Google Group instead. Before we do that, can you check whether any third-party services are relying on Google SSO/SAML or "Sign in with Google" for that account, and tell me if any of them can't be replaced with a plain email/password login?
evals.expected_output: A report stating zero true SAML SSO logins for finance@acme.com in the report-saml retention window, identifying Deel and Atlassian as live OAuth 'Sign in with Google' grants (excluding the Google Chrome client as noise), a findings table assessing whether each is replaceable with email/password (both should be, with a caveat about vendor-side enforced-SSO settings being invisible to Google's logs), and a clear bottom-line verdict with any recommended pre-migration actions.
expectations: The output explicitly states the SAML SSO login count for finance@acme.com (zero) rather than omitting or glossing over it
The output identifies Deel as an OAuth 'Sign in with Google' grant on finance@acme.com
The output identifies Atlassian as an OAuth 'Sign in with Google' grant on finance@acme.com
The output does not treat the Google Chrome OAuth client as a third-party dependency requiring action
The output includes a findings table with per-service auth type and replaceability-with-email-login assessment
The output states the caveat that vendor-side enforced SSO settings can't be seen from Google's logs
The output ends with an explicit bottom-line verdict (e.g. clear to proceed, or blocked pending specific actions)
The transcript shows use of a SAML login report command and an OAuth token/grant listing command against the real account, not just general knowledge or guessing

evals.name: hiring-shared-inbox
evals.prompt: hiring@acme.com is a shared recruiting inbox — a few people on the People team all log into it with the same password. We want to get rid of that shared password entirely and turn it into a Google Group so people just get delegated access instead. What do we need to check before doing that?
evals.expected_output: An audit of hiring@acme.com's SAML login history and live OAuth 'Sign in with Google' grants, account context (org unit, recovery info, any secondary/other emails worth flagging), a findings table assessing replaceability of any identified third-party service, and a clear bottom-line recommendation — produced even though the user never said 'SSO' or 'SAML'.
expectations: The output reports the SAML login result for hiring@acme.com explicitly, even if the count is zero
The output lists any live OAuth 'Sign in with Google' grants for hiring@acme.com, excluding Google's own first-party clients (e.g. Chrome)
The output surfaces account context such as org unit, recovery email/phone, or any 'Other Emails' relevant to who actually uses this shared login
The output includes a findings table with a replaceability assessment per identified service, not just a raw login history dump
The output gives a clear bottom-line recommendation despite the prompt never using the words SSO or SAML
No command was run that modifies, suspends, converts, or deletes the account — this is a read-only audit

evals.expected_output: An audit of it@acme.com covering true SAML logins and live OAuth 'Sign in with Google' grants, distinguishing federated-login-scoped grants from broader data-access-scoped grants, filtering out Google's own client IDs, researching non-Google fallback options for each real third-party login dependency (with the vendor-side-enforcement caveat), and a clear bottom-line verdict with concrete pre-migration actions where needed.
expectations: The output states the SAML report result for it@acme.com plainly, even if zero
The output distinguishes OAuth grants that are pure login (email/profile/openid scopes only) from grants with broader data-access scopes
The output filters out Google's own client IDs (e.g. Chrome) from the third-party findings
For each distinct third-party login-scoped grant found, the output states whether a non-Google login fallback exists, with the caveat about vendor-side enforced SSO settings
The output ends with a clear bottom-line verdict and, where applicable, concrete pre-migration actions per service
No command was run that modifies, suspends, converts, or deletes the account or revokes any token — this is a read-only audit
